Which Spanish opera about Don Quixote was staged by Bodo Igesz, and how many acts does it have?

Bodo Igesz (February 7, 1935, Amsterdam - December 25, 2014, Manhattan) was a Dutch stage director who had an active career staging operas around the world during the second half of the 20th century.  He was particularly known for his work with the Metropolitan Opera where he worked for 25 years on the staging staff.  He also staged operas for the Salzburg Festival, and staged numerous operas for the Santa Fe Opera; including the United States premieres of Hindemith's "Cardillac" (1967), Schoenberg's "Die Jakobsleiter" (1968), Henze's "The Bassarids" (1968) and Aribert Reimann's "Melusine" (1972).

The passages identify three operas with Don Quixote themes: the Massenet "Don Quichotte" (French libretto), the Telemann "Don Quichotte auf der Hochzeit des Comacho" (German), and the Hervé "Don Quichotte et Sancho Pança" (French). None are identified as Spanish operas.

Although "El retablo de maese Pedro" by Manuel de Falla is a Spanish opera about Don Quixote with fewer acts than a standard full-length opera, the passages contain no information about Bodo Igesz staging this work or any other Spanish Don Quixote opera.
